reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
clinicalPearls: Caused by deficiency of succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH5A1), the second enzyme of GABA degradation, so succinic semialdehyde is diverted to gamma-hydroxybutyric acid (GHB)

The diagnostic biochemical hallmark is accumulation of 4-hydroxybutyric acid (gamma-hydroxybutyrate) in urine, plasma, and CSF, which is not detected on routine organic acid screening unless specifically sought
Typical features are global developmental delay, prominent expressive language delay, hypotonia, ataxia, and behavioural/psychiatric problems, with epilepsy in many
Both GABA and GHB accumulate, and the balance of GABA-B and GHB receptor effects is thought to explain the mixed excitatory and sedative neurological picture
Brain MRI often shows a characteristic symmetric high T2 signal in the globus pallidus, subthalamic nuclei, and dentate nuclei

It is generally a slowly progressive or static encephalopathy rather than an acute metabolic crisis illness; management is supportive and antiepileptic, with vigabatrin used cautiously given theoretical benefit and risk
British spelling and paediatric context apply
reference.pathophysiology: The inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA is catabolised via GABA transaminase to succinic semialdehyde, which succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase then oxidises to succinate for entry into the citric acid cycle. When this enzyme is deficient, succinic semialdehyde is instead reduced to gamma-hydroxybutyrate (GHB), which accumulates along with GABA in the brain and body fluids. GHB and elevated GABA act on GHB and GABA-B receptors, disturbing neurotransmission in ways that produce the developmental, motor, epileptic, and behavioural manifestations. The build-up of these neuroactive compounds, rather than an energy-failure crisis, characterises the disorder, giving a comparatively static or slowly evolving encephalopathy.
additionalDifferentials: Other causes of global developmental delay with prominent language impairment
Mitochondrial disorders with bilateral pallidal signal change
GHB ingestion or intoxication (acquired) as a mimic of the biochemistry
additionalInvestigations: Urine organic acids with specific detection of 4-hydroxybutyric acid (may be missed on standard screens)
Quantification of gamma-hydroxybutyrate in plasma and CSF
Brain MRI for symmetric globus pallidus, subthalamic, and dentate signal change
Enzyme activity assay in leucocytes or lymphocytes
Molecular analysis of the ALDH5A1 gene
redFlags: Worsening seizures or status epilepticus requiring urgent management
Significant neuropsychiatric deterioration or behavioural crisis
Regression or unexpected rapid decline prompting reassessment
Suspected GHB intoxication needing differentiation from the inherited disorder
reference.prognosis: The course is usually that of a static or slowly progressive encephalopathy with intellectual disability, language impairment, and variable epilepsy; many survive into adulthood. Outcome varies, and behavioural and psychiatric symptoms can be prominent later.
pitfalls: Missing the diagnosis because 4-hydroxybutyrate is not reliably seen on routine organic acid analysis
Confusing the biochemical finding with exogenous GHB exposure
Using antiepileptic agents without regard to the disturbed GABA metabolism
references: Scriver's OMMBID: succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency and GABA metabolism
Nyhan, Atlas of Inherited Metabolic Diseases
management: Manage epilepsy with antiepileptic drugs, avoiding valproate which may further inhibit residual enzyme activity
Consider cautious vigabatrin to lower gamma-hydroxybutyrate, balanced against its risk of visual field loss
Treat behavioural and psychiatric symptoms with appropriate psychotropic agents alongside behavioural support
Provide developmental support with physiotherapy, occupational therapy and speech and language therapy for delay, hypotonia and ataxia
Monitor with EEG for seizures and, when vigabatrin is used, regular ophthalmological visual field assessment
Offer genetic counselling and family testing given autosomal recessive inheritance of ALDH5A1 variants
Coordinate care through a metabolic medicine and neurology multidisciplinary team
